confounds: The harness runtime (harnesses/python/runtime.py) runs inside the program's interpreter process. It imports marshal, os, sys, threading and time (and, through threading, _collections, _weakrefset, itertools, types and warnings) before the program starts, so a program's own import of these runs no module code and counts no instructions.

The program's module is exec'd under three runtime frames, not run as the interpreter's own script: about three fewer frames are available before RecursionError at the default recursion limit (1000, not changed).
Two runtime threads (control and watcher) run beside the program in every configuration; neither runs program code (except finalizers run by gc.collect() in storage mode) and neither is counted.

The budget counter is the step meter (sys.monitoring INSTRUCTION) in every mode, behaviour included (harnesses/QUESTIONS.md Q17); a computation is stopped at its budget by pausing its thread inside the monitoring callback, never by an exception.

The instructions of the program's own H call sites are counted as the program's; those executed inside the H calls are not, nor those of the traceback module while it formats an uncaught exception (instruction events are switched off then if no other computation is running; a thread the program started that is still running is not counted meanwhile).
Spawned computations run in threads the runtime starts; in core and extended one after another, in stdlib-concurrency side by side.

The end of a stage is read from the program (its next cp.stage(), its end, its budget, its error) or from quiescence: every running computation alive and executing no instruction for 0.5 s, sampled by wall clock (README.md, section 6).
Answers are what the program passes to cp.answer(), which prints them as print() would; answers after the cap are printed but not collected.
observe() reads only the objects the program registered, rendered by an iterative equivalent of repr(); the states alternatives pending and suspended come only from registrations.
In storage mode tracemalloc (1 frame, started before the program) traces the runtime's own allocations during the stage with the program's, and gc.collect() runs at each stage boundary.
Standard output and standard error are files; the runtime flushes sys.stdout and sys.stderr at every stage boundary.
P13's CPU time and maximum resident set size are the whole interpreter process's (resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF)), runtime threads included.
A thread a program starts with _thread.start_new_thread directly, not through threading.Thread, is not attributed to any computation and its instructions are not counted.

The program is compiled from its text with the constants block's lines emptied, and its constants are given to it as s.constants with their stage (README.md 3.1); tracebacks show that text, not the file on disk.

execution_state.basis: the instruction budget ran out: the computation's thread is paused in the sys.monitoring callback at exactly its budget

alternatives.unit: entries of the program's registered pending structures (cp.pending)

suspended.unit: entries of the program's registered waiting structures (cp.suspended)
